clue.text: Those who pay, putting paid to betting odds

parts.note: SP stands for starting price, the odds at which a racing bet is settled
people putting paid to things are finishers of them, so enders

explanation.surface: A description of punters whose losses finish off their chances at the bookmaker's.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Putting paid to' reads as part of the paying definition, but it means finishing off, so it gives the people who finish things; the betting odds are the racing starting price.
explanation.definitionFit: Anyone who lays out money on purchases is someone who pays.

clue.text: Minimal clothing supplied by sempstress

definitions.meaning: as in 'not a ... on', wearing nothing
what a seamstress puts in with a needle

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase 'not a stitch on' means naked, and a seamstress sews single loops of thread.

clue.text: It's intolerable to be past it

definitions.text: It's intolerable to be past it

parts.words: It's intolerable to be past it
parts.note: something beyond what one can bear is intolerable; 'past it' seems to mean too old

explanation.definitionFit: Something past bearing is beyond one's capacity to put up with hardship.

clue.text: Cause despondency by placing record in cover

indicators.note: in places the record inside the word for cover

parts.note: a dress covers the body
EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: Putting a disc in a sleeve somehow makes one gloomy.
explanation.definitionFit: To make someone low in spirits or dejected.

clue.text: The Right finishes in tears

parts.note: finishes are ends

explanation.surface: A right-wing party collapses in weeping.
explanation.definitionFit: Rips apart, the verb tears pronounced to rhyme with bears.

clue.text: Ace pressman looked astonished

parts.note: an ace performer is a star
ED is short for editor, a newspaper man

explanation.surface: A top journalist gazes in amazement at something.
explanation.definitionFit: Gazing wide-eyed in amazement is how someone looks when astonished.

clue.text: Stopped trying at Twickenham ?

parts.note: in rugby an opponent stopped from scoring a try was brought down; 'stopped trying' also suggests giving up

explanation.walkthrough: Twickenham is England's national rugby ground in south-west London.
explanation.definitionFit: In rugby, a player carrying the ball is halted by being brought down.

clue.text: Bones in dairies are uncommonly pointless

indicators.note: done uncommonly means arranged in an unusual way, so the remaining letters are shuffled
points are compass directions, so being pointless means losing the letters for east and south

explanation.surface: Bones found in dairy farms are rarely blunt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pointless' drops E and S (compass points) from DAIRIES, leaving DAIRI, which 'uncommonly' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural of the forearm bone on the thumb side.

clue.text: Adder may disturb one's light reverie

indicators.note: to disturb something is to mess it about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A snake might interrupt someone's gentle musing.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleasant fantasy indulged while awake is a light reverie.

clue.text: Help Old Contemptibles in red cataclysm

parts.note: the British Expeditionary Force of 1914, abbreviated BEF, nicknamed the Old Contemptibles

indicators.note: a cataclysm is an upheaval, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: First World War soldiers caught up in a bloody disaster need assistance.
explanation.walkthrough: BEF is followed by the letters of IN RED rearranged by 'cataclysm'.
explanation.definitionFit: To act as a friend to someone in need is to assist them.

clue.text: American festival piece ended with Danny in disarray

indicators.note: things in disarray are jumbled up, so these three words have their letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A musical piece for an American celebration finishes in a mess with someone called Danny.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of PIECE, ENDED and DANNY, linked by 'with', are rearranged as 'in disarray' signals.
explanation.definitionFit: The Fourth of July holiday marks the 1776 declaration that freed the colonies from Britain.

clue.text: Scottish sportsmen get in a girl's hair

definitions.meaning: players of the ice game with stones and brooms, popular in Scotland
rollers put in hair to give it waves

explanation.definitionFit: Players of the stone-sliding ice sport share their name with hair rollers.

clue.text: Monte Carlo driver recovering his strength ?

definitions.meaning: a competitor in the Monte Carlo Rally, a famous motor rally
someone who rallies regains vigour after illness

explanation.definitionFit: A motor-rally competitor and one who recovers strength both take their name from the verb meaning to come back.

clue.text: Unusual taste in oriental liqueur

indicators.note: something unusual is out of the ordinary, so the letters of these words are rearranged

parts.note: E is short for eastern, so oriental

explanation.surface: Someone notes an odd flavour in a drink from the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusual' rearranges TASTE IN; E for oriental goes at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: An aniseed-flavoured sweet cordial is a type of liqueur.

clue.text: Arthur Lord gets cross with New York boy

parts.note: X, a cross, is the Roman numeral for ten
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A nobleman called Arthur is annoyed with a lad from New York.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points to the Victorian poet laureate made a lord, who wrote of King Arthur in Idylls of the King.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victorian peer-poet whose Idylls of the King retold Arthurian legend.

clue.text: She's a help coming back

indicators.note: returning means these words are read backwards

parts.note: a help is an aid, written as two words

explanation.surface: A woman is described as useful on her return.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's given name, here clued by the female pronoun.

clue.text: Openings for a saucy sort of ruse

parts.note: pert means cheeky or saucy

indicators.note: sort of means rearranged, as if sorting the letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Gaps that allow a cheeky trick.
explanation.definitionFit: Holes or gaps through which light or things pass.

clue.text: What man does may be disposed of by higher authority

definitions.text: What man does may be disposed of by higher authority

parts.words: What man does may be disposed of by higher authority
parts.note: alludes to the proverb that man suggests plans but God decides them

explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says man suggests a plan while God decides its outcome.

clue.text: Governor tucked into spirit of rhubarb

indicators.note: one thing tucked into another sits inside it, so these letters go within the spirit

parts.note: rum is a spirit distilled from sugar cane
HE is His Excellency, the title of a colonial governor

explanation.surface: An official is put inside a rhubarb-flavoured spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: HE (His Excellency, a governor's title) is tucked into RUM.
explanation.definitionFit: The botanical genus name for the rhubarb plant.

clue.text: Dance in the yard, say

definitions.meaning: a stately dance, an old sense of the word
a yard is one unit for gauging length

explanation.definitionFit: A stately dance and a unit for gauging size share one word.

clue.text: Constructs tree dwelling, if in trouble inside

indicators.note: letters in trouble are disturbed, so the words either side are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone builds a treehouse in case things go wrong indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in trouble' stands between its two fodder words, and 'inside' looks like a container signal but is simply letters to shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: To build a nest, as birds do, is to make a dwelling in a tree.

clue.text: Crumbly like chips ?

definitions.meaning: punning: chips can be fried, so fry-able

explanation.definitionFit: Easily crumbled soil, and punningly suitable for frying like potatoes.

clue.text: Beamish boy, retired, made asinine comment

annotationWithheld.why: Beamish boy, retired, made asinine comment (6): RAY (beamish boy) in BED, but 'retired' must be both BED and the container signal
annotationWithheld.clue: Beamish boy, retired, made asinine comment

clue.text: Electoral system one queen finds original

parts.note: PR is proportional representation, a voting system
I is the Roman numeral for one
Mary is the name of several English and Scottish queens

explanation.surface: A voting method lets a single monarch discover something novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Electoral system' looks like the definition, but it gives PR; 'original' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Something first or earliest in a series is primal, the earliest form.

clue.text: Picture one game that went wrong

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: letters that went wrong are out of order, so these are rearranged

explanation.surface: A photo of a match that turned out badly.
explanation.definitionFit: A likeness or representation such as a photograph.

clue.text: Write cunningly about a way to cheat

indicators.note: about means around, so the rearranged letters go outside the road abbreviation
done cunningly means rearranged with craft, so the letters of this word are shuffled

parts.note: ST is street, a way

explanation.walkthrough: 'cunningly' turns the first word into TWIER, which 'about' wraps round the street abbreviation; 'a' and 'to' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A swindler or deceiver, especially in British slang, is a dishonest operator.

clue.text: Blooming impertinence of organized labour!

parts.note: TU is a trade union, organized labour
lip is cheeky talk

explanation.surface: An exasperated outburst about union cheek.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blooming' seems a mild British expletive but defines a flowering plant; the pieces come in answer order, TU then LIP.
explanation.definitionFit: A spring bulb flower is something seen blooming in gardens.

clue.text: French free gift to those celebrating 10

definitions.text: French free gift to those celebrating 10

parts.words: French free gift to those celebrating 10
parts.note: a present from France to the people who mark the July holiday of 10 across, a famous figure of freedom

explanation.definitionFit: France gave the United States the New York harbour monument in 1886.

clue.text: Put to bed, like some tennis players?

definitions.meaning: ranked in a draw so the best players avoid each other early

explanation.definitionFit: Sowing a garden plot and ranking top players in a tournament draw share one word.

clue.text: Mollified and relaxed after a very quiet start

indicators.note: after means the relaxing piece follows the opening ones

parts.note: PP is pianissimo, very quiet in music
eased means loosened or relaxed

explanation.surface: Someone was calmed and loosened up following a hushed beginning.
explanation.definitionFit: Calmed or placated someone's anger.
